seat.BEST_WHY: The floor stonework in the lit band around the figure is genuinely cut, not stamped: directly below and right of the figure (roughly x 440–640, y 440–600) there is one long pale slab beside a run of half-size squares, joint lines shift between 1px and 3px along the same run, and two long cracks (one from ~(240,470) to ~(500,510), one arcing at bottom-right ~(560,700)→(750,650)) cross stone boundaries instead of stopping at tile edges. The light does what the brief says — the stones go from pale cream at the figure to near-black at the room's edges with no visible tile-quantised steps — and the corridor at x 500–560 reads as a real gap in the wall band rather than a painted-on opening. It is also the only frame in the shared scene where nothing has been placed on the floor that breaks the projection.
seat.WORST_WHY: Every surface is a fill, not a drawing. The dirt floor (x 55–250, y 0–215) is a single cellular-noise texture — dark red-brown cell edges with blue-grey flecks — repeated across ~7×6 tiles with no structure, wear, or path. The pool (x 250–345, y 0–190) is a flat teal with a visible repeating hexagon pattern under it and green circles-with-a-cross for lily pads. The grey stone tiles in the left corridor (x 20–55) are identical repeats with a 1px grid; the "moss" is the same soft teal blob pasted at half opacity at (~15–45, 55–85), (~15–40, 205–230) and (~350–380, 145–175). There is no light model at all — the frame is uniformly lit from nowhere — so nothing has volume; the barrels at (~110–195, 195–215) and the chests are the only things with any edge shading. It is internally consistent (all props are top-down, and the orc at (~215,5) is the only figure in any frame with a contact shadow), but it is a free tileset, not a made place.

panel.ruling: five seats; block only on strong-majority regression (>=4 of 5 rank below the reference); else install if exit met and plant caught. Rank-in-deck cannot resolve polish-sized deltas at a 40% flip rate. — Rafe, 2026-09-09
panel.law: a gate's binding term must have a measured noise floor and must never be a single sample. — Rafe, 2026-09-08

_what: THE ITEM'S OWN MEASURED EXIT — required by INSTALL-LATEST (Rafe, 2026-09-08).
A build installs because it DID THE THING IT SET OUT TO DO. The rank test only says
the doing cost nothing against the seeded reference; this says what was done. Without
it, 'not worse than the reference' would mean 'not different from it', and a round
that changed nothing would install as readily as one that fixed something.
Declared here per item, recorded into the verdict, re-checked at the gate. The gate
refuses a `met` with no measurement behind it.
